systems: EU AI Act Annex III high-risk systems (hiring, credit scoring, insurance, policing, education, border control)
Palantir Gotham / VeRA police data mining (Bavaria, Art. 61a BayPAG)
Jobcenter / Bundesagentur für Arbeit automation and data matching
highlights: Digital Omnibus on AI delays Annex III high-risk obligations from 2 Aug 2026 to 2 Dec 2027 (Annex I to 2 Aug 2028); non-retroactivity under Art. 111 means pre-deadline systems may escape indefinitely, public-authority systems only caught from 31 Dec 2030.
Art. 50 AI Act transparency duties (chatbot disclosure, AI content labelling) still apply from 2 Aug 2026; grace period for existing systems under Art. 50(2) until 2 Dec 2026.

GFF filed a constitutional complaint against Art. 61a BayPAG allowing Palantir-based police data mining (VeRA) in Bavaria; builds on BVerfG ruling of 16 Feb 2023 striking down § 25a HSOG and § 49 HmbPolDVG.

CJEU: credit-agency scoring can be an automated individual decision under Art. 22(1) GDPR; VG Wiesbaden granted a broad Art. 15(1)(h) access right after a loan refusal based on a 85.96 % SCHUFA score.

Federal commission welfare-reform recommendations criticised by netzpolitik.org as a rollback of fundamental rights; Bundesagentur für Arbeit projects over 610,000 Jobcenter appeals in 2026, one in four successful.
actions_taken: web research on EU AI Act omnibus delay, Bavarian police data mining, SCHUFA scoring under Art. 22 GDPR, Jobcenter automation
